# Local compute pool
English | 中文

A **DeepSeek Harness plugin** that pools several local inference endpoints into one compute pool:
de

legated subagents are spread across the machines by load, every endpoint has its own concurrency
gat

e and queue, a failing endpoint is parked and the next attempt fails over — and when no local
endpoi
nt is usable, children keep the route the harness resolved.

* Package: `dsh-local-compute-pool` · Card title: **Local compute pool** / 本地算力池
* Distribution: a *

*plain directory bundle** (not an npm package) — clone this repository and install
it by absolute pa

th, as described below
* License: MIT
## What it solves
A locally served model has three hard limits, and every mechanism here maps to one of them:
| Reality of local inference | What the plugin does |
| VRAM/RAM is limited — usually one conversation at a time | A per-endpoint **concurrency gate** (de
fault 1): at most `concurrency` requests at once, the rest queue (with a depth limit and a timeout)

|
| Context caching is weak | Each subagent is **pinned to one machine for its whole life**, so the

prompt prefix and the tool-call dialect stay stable |
| Parallel requests are handled poorly | The `
least-busy` strategy spreads subagents across machines instead of stacking them behind one |
The point is not "going faster" — it is **turning "start several subagents" from unusable into usabl

e**
on local models: a local server that receives two concurrent requests often does not run each at

half
speed, it times out on both or blows up its VRAM.
## You may be stuck exactly here

Picture this: you own a few good GPUs. Running an LLM under a framework such as
Strata or
NInfer giv

es you speed and quality you are happy with.
You are not short of computers — but a consumer motherb

oard usually has only two PCIe slots, so you
cannot fit them all into one machine, and therefore can

not make them work on one task **at the same
time**.

The bottleneck was never raw compute. It is that the compute sits in several separate computers,
eac

s never raw compute. It is that the compute sits in several separate computers,
each fighting alone.
**Local compute pool was written for exactly that.** It lets models on different computers take part

in the same task as delegated subagents: the main agent splits the work, the plugin places the
resu
lting subagents on the available machines to run in parallel, and the results are gathered back.

This is how I use it: one machine with a 5090 and one with dual 4080S cards, each running Qwen 3.8
F

lash Next at roughly 100 tok/s. With this plugin, two subagents of the same task land on the two
mac

hines and proceed at once — **about 200 tok/s of combined effective throughput**, as if the two
comp
uters had been soldered into the single machine your slots could not hold.
> To be precise: this does not make a **single generation** faster — autoregressive decoding cannot
> add two streams of tokens together. It makes **several subagents inside one task truly parallel**,
> so total throughput stacks.
## The two lists on the settings page
The settings page is built around two lists with clearly separate jobs:
1. **Trigger whitelist** — marks **which models may enable this plugin**. Only when a task's own mod

el
runs on a whitelisted provider are its subagents handed to the local pool; tasks that are not tic

ked
are untouched and keep the route the harness resolved.
2. **Subagent model pool** — lists **whic

h machines/endpoints offer compute**. Each endpoint gets its
own concurrency, and the plugin spreads
subagents across them by load.
## Requirements

* DeepSeek Harness desktop (developed and verified on `0.2.0-rc.2`).
* At least one local OpenAI-com

patible provider already configured in `llm-pi-ai` (for example
`local` → `http://127.0.0.1:8888/v1`

). The plugin sends no HTTP of its own and adds no provider:
it only decides *who* and queues.
## Install

Two steps, and that is all: **no npm, no build step, no dependencies.** This repository is a plain
d
irectory bundle — cloning it gives you everything the plugin needs.
Clone this repository:
[代码示例省略，未执行]
Then install the `plugin` directory by its **absolute path**:
[代码示例省略，未执行]

> Not on npm, on purpose: publishing would add a registry account and a republish-on-every-change
>
ritual, in exchange for saving one `git clone`. See docs/DESIGN.en.md.
Afterwards:
* the package joins the profile's `dsh.profile.bundles`, and this repository's `plugin/cordis.patch.

if it reports `restart-required`, restart the desktop app;
* later edits to `cordis.patch.yml`'s `c

onfig` are reloaded by HMR, while **editing JavaScript
(`index.js` / `lib/*` / `client.js`) needs a
restart** (the browser half only needs a page refresh).
Remove it with `plugin_manager action: remove_bundle target: dsh-local-compute-pool`.
## First run

1. **Add endpoints**: sidebar **Plugins** → card **Local compute pool** → *Subagent model pool* →
*+

Add a local endpoint*. Pick the `provider` from the live directory, choose `auto` (the first
model

that provider advertises) or an exact id, and set `concurrency` to how many requests that
machine se

rves at once (1 for a single-session local server).
**The shipped endpoint list is empty**: a defaul

t pointing at a service that does not exist on
someone else's machine can only fail, so none is pres

et.
2. **Decide who may use local compute**: tick providers in the *Trigger whitelist*. Only tasks w

hose
own model runs on those providers hand their subagents to the local pool; an empty whitelist me

ans
"no restriction". The number beside each entry is that task's subagent cap: it is written into t

he
task's prompt and **enforced** at the stream gate (counted per task, across machines).
3. **Verif

y**: start two subagents in one message — they should land on different endpoints. Or have
the model

call the `local_pool` tool to see in-flight / queued / parked counts per machine, how
many slots a
task holds for itself, and each task's subagent budget.
